paragraphs.source_en: On rising, Ogin, widow of the Y Yorozuya house, opened the window and looked at the sky outside. This grand tea gathering was unprecedented not only for Hideyoshi; for Ogin's adoptive father, the lay priest Rikyū, hailed as the great tea master, it was also a momentous day that would define his life's achievement. Rikyū would naturally direct the entire affair, and nearly all those assisting him were disciples who revered him as their master. Rikyū therefore went frequently to Fushin-an at Jurakudai to attend to every detail.

paragraphs.source_en: At about the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Horse, the tea service ended. Next came an unprecedented tour by the Regent. Behind Hideyoshi and Ieyasu, who personally served tea to the guests, came a company of court nobles and daimyos, all smiling broadly. They reached a corner of the commoners' enclosure and stopped at Yorozuya Sōan's stall.
